correctness.rationale: PASS: The original proof counts crossed vertical and two horizontal base-edge families exactly. For generic planes the n+2 side maximum is equivalent to exactly one projected vertex above and below the axial normal threshold. Odd base order leads to two offset extreme-angle order statistics, and on α∈[0,π/(2n)] the event is cos(δ+α)<S<cos(δ-α); the uniformly sampled normal gives CDF P(S<=x)=x/sqrt(h²+x²). Integrating this angular gap produces exactly the three-term arcsine formula. Independent 50-digit quadrature matched the analytic expression for odd n=5,7,11,25 and several h to 40 digits. Differentiating in t=(1+h²)^(-1/2), sine strict concavity gives positive derivative at t=0 and tangent strict convexity negative at t=1. For n>=5, sin^k is convex over [δ/2,3δ/2] for all odd k>=3 because sin²(3π/10)<2/3; its positive-coefficient series makes the derivative strictly decreasing and establishes unique optimum. Uniform Taylor expansion gives p_n(h)=π²t(1-t²)/(2n²)+O(n^-4); maximizing yields π²/(3sqrt3) and h→sqrt2. Boundary measure-zero nongeneric planes excluded correctly; finite tests supplement the universal proof.

final_claim: For every odd n>=5, a central plane section of a right regular n-gonal prism has at most n+2 sides, with explicit Haar probability p_n(h)=(2n/π)(2H_h(π/n)-H_h(π/(2n))-H_h(3π/(2n))). This is positive for h>0, has a unique optimal aspect ratio, and sup_h n²p_n(h)→π²/(3√3) at h→√2, half the even-base coefficient.
limitations: Only generic central planes, uniformly oriented normals, and exactly regular right odd prisms n>=5; no translated-plane distributions.
